introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, "Answer all Questions"): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
incertitudes: Question 11 : en 11(c) les repères (i) et (ii) sont imprimés sur une même ligne, avec les marques « (4 marks) » et « (3 marks) » en colonne ; ils sont lus comme (i) = 4 marques (schéma) et (ii) = 3 marques (trois fonctions). En 11(a), « (4 mark) » est imprimé sans « s ». Les marques par bloc donnent 4 + 4 + (4 + 3) = 15, conformes au « Total 15 marks » imprimé ; `points` : a = 4, b = 4, c = 7.

Question 11(b) : le point proche normal (25 cm) n'est pas donné ; il est retenu pour calculer la lentille correctrice (f = 33,3 cm, soit + 3,0 dioptries). Les schémas demandés en (b) et (c) sont à tracer par le candidat et sont décrits.

questions.enonce_markdown: Compare X-rays and ultrasound in medical diagnosis *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| | X-rays | Ultrasound |
|---|---|---|
| Nature | **Electromagnetic waves** (transverse), very short wavelength; can travel in a vacuum | **Mechanical (sound) waves**, longitudinal, of frequency above $20\ \mathrm{kHz}$ (typically $1$ to $15\ \mathrm{MHz}$); need a medium |
| How the image forms | Differential **absorption**: dense tissue (bone) absorbs more, so the shadow is recorded on film or a detector | Partial **reflection (echoes)** at boundaries between tissues of different acoustic impedance, detected and displayed as an image (scan) |
| Best used for | Bones, fractures, teeth, chest (lungs), and soft tissue with a contrast medium (barium meal) | **Soft tissues** and organs: foetus in pregnancy, heart, liver, kidneys |
| Safety | **Ionising radiation**: can damage cells or cause cancer, so the dose must be limited and it is avoided in pregnancy | **Non-ionising**: considered safe, so it can be used repeatedly and on the foetus |
| Image and cost | Static image, high resolution of bone; equipment more costly and bulky | **Real-time** (moving) image; cheaper and portable equipment |

questions.enonce_markdown: A person's near point is $100\ \mathrm{cm}$. Explain using a diagram how the defect can be corrected. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**The defect.** The near point of a normal eye is about $25\ \mathrm{cm}$. A person whose near point is $100\ \mathrm{cm}$ cannot see clearly objects closer than $1\ \mathrm{m}$: this is **long sight (hypermetropia)**, caused by an eyeball that is too short or by a lens that is too weak. Light from a near object is focused **behind the retina**.

**Correction.** The person wears a **converging (convex) lens**. It must form a **virtual, upright image at $100\ \mathrm{cm}$ (the person's near point)** of an object placed at the normal near point, $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the eye. The eye then sees that image clearly.

**Diagram (to be drawn by the candidate).** Draw the eye, a convex lens in front of it, and an object O at $25\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the lens (inside the focal length). Two rays from the top of O: one parallel to the principal axis, refracted through the focus F; one through the centre of the lens, undeviated. The refracted rays diverge, and their backward extensions (dotted lines) meet at the **virtual image I, $100\ \mathrm{cm}$ from the lens on the same side as the object**, larger than the object. The diverging rays enter the eye and appear to come from I.

**Focal length of the lens** (real-is-positive convention, virtual image $v = -100\ \mathrm{cm}$, $u = 25\ \mathrm{cm}$):
$$\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{u} + \frac{1}{v} = \frac{1}{25} - \frac{1}{100} = \frac{3}{100}\ \mathrm{cm^{-1}}\ \Rightarrow\ f = 33.3\ \mathrm{cm}$$
The lens is a **converging lens of focal length about $33\ \mathrm{cm}$ (power $+3.0\ \mathrm{D}$)**.
